Also available at: http://aappolicy.aappublications.org/cgi/content/full/ pediatrics%3b108/3/776 (accessed 25/05/04) Effects on the biliary tract. Using abdominal ultrasonogra- phy, biliary sludge or pseudolithiasis was found in about 40% of severely ill children being treated with high doses of ceftriaxone1 and was later reported in adults.2-4 The sludge has been identified as a calcium salt of ceftriaxone.5 Patients are often asymptomatic and the sludge usually dissolves once ceftriaxone is stopped. Gallstones with ceftriaxone as a major component have been identified in a patient given long-term high-dose treatment.6 Similarly, a bile-duct stone composed of ceftriaxone occurred with high-dose ceftriaxone in a child.7 In another report, intrac- table hiccups were associated with ceftriaxone-related pseudo- lithiasis in a 10-year-old boy.8 1.
